reviews.comment: lectures are like melatonin to an insomniac. he makes many mistakes during lecture, its not worth listening to just do homework during class. exams are super easy, just make sure to study the exam review and textbook concepts. homeworks can get quite difficult and long so start on them asap, but the late day system is a lifesaver.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Attendance is mandatory and his accent can make it hard to understand him in the lectures, but hes a kind professor and grades fairly. The tests are not difficult, as long as you can complete the homework and pay attention to the content.

Lectures are mostly reading off the slides, which most overlook, but looking at the lecture slides and making sure you understand them as you go is very very helpful for exam prep. The TAs for this class are the GOATS. Start your hw early.
He was just alright, mostly read off the slides during lectures. There was a quiz every lecture and lectures 3x a week.

Going to lectures is helpful mostly for exam review. All the contents you need to learn are in slide shows (which are pretty much the lectures) and readings. You kinda only learn coding by doing it, in lab and homework. The homework gets pretty hard sometimes and it's the most annoying thing to me. Ask him more questions to get more from him.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Hes doing his job. Lecturing a programming language class is inherently a very ineffective way to learn/teach.
Homework takes forever, in class quiz every day so attendance is mandatory, extremely boring lectures and almost no one is paying attention, but he is a knowledgeable and nice guy.

Absolutely not. Go take the course with another professor. The class is not hard by any means, but easy to lose track of if juggling other difficult courses. Lectures are boring, not engaging at all. He will not post your grades on Canvas, and you will not know your score for most of the class. Homework takes forever, too!
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Overall it was meh. He's really nice and chill but his lectures were pretty boring since he would just read off the slides. I only went to class because we had a quiz everyday and he probably just did that to make sure people would go to class. Everything was pretty much straight from the slides so if you study those you should be fine.
I'm kinda bad at cs but his lectures are ok not very engaging but still good enough. Exams are pretty hard.

He was alr. His lectures were a bit on the slower side, but he got through the required ppts on time (by the end of your 80 mins or wtvr). If you ask questions he'll answer them thoroughly. His speech is a bit monotonous so j grab a coffee or monster before you head on in. Fairly simple Canvas quizzes at the end of each lecture, nthn to worry abt.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: He reads off the slides mumbling while the slides themselves aren't informative, leaving me googling often. He rushes through the slides to give quizzes and there were so many it became annoying attendance checks. The quizzes aren't helpful as the test reviews they post are better. 120 is standardized so no benefit to put up with him, profs matter.

Yes, professors don't matter for this course. That being said, stay away from him if possible. GENUINELY impossible to pay attention to a word he says his teaching style is so boring. You'll teach yourself what you need to know, which isn't bad. Exam reviews and practice exams are saviors. Also ChatGPT. Homeworks take SO LONG but are free grades.
reviews.ratingTags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment:
I just wish lectures were a bit more structured, and we could actually tell what material is important. There were many days that were just a review of very easy concepts, and some difficult material was covered without any depth, and maybe only once.
It took me until halfway through the semester to even find the slides.

Leyk was monotone and just read word for word off of the slides we already had access to. Im not actually sure he knows anything about C++. If you have any questions, too bad because he is going to leave class early while you're working on your daily end of class quiz. Taught myself the entire class.

The class itself is mostly homework and self learning and the professor doesn't matter much. He's a pretty boring lecturer but he's chill. They give quizzes every class so people don't just skip the lectures. Most people skip them anyways though but he's a chill guy.

His lectures are pretty boring and there's a class activity every class so you have to show up. Relatively easy class so prof doesn't really matter. You can access every prof's materials on canvas too.

I didn't really listen to his lecture because of his accent, but he was always nice and forgiving whenever you had a problem with something. Pretty easy exam despite me not really listening. If you know how to do the labs or have coding experience, you will do good on his assignments/exams!

Dr. Leyk is very knowledgeable and caring. He explains C programming clearly, often asks if anyone has questions, and makes an effort to be personable though older. Labs reinforce material, and short end-of-class quizzes aren't too hard but keep you engaged. Fair grading and supportive.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professors don't matter much for this course. Most people don't attend lectures because of how boring they can be, but Leyk is pretty helpful regardless. He's pretty chill too.

120 profs don't matter too much. Leyk's lectures were boring and people stop going after a while, but it's still a manageable class since homeworks are worth as much as exams. Because people stop going to class, he gives like two quizzes every class about previous lectures but they end up only being completion. He's chill though. I'd recommend.

Prof honestly doesnt matter too much for 120. Leyk is very nice and gives alright lectures, its pretty hard to stay focused but lectures do help if you can manage to lock in on what he is saying. 120 has lots of homework, but if you use the PTs the class becomes 10x easier. Exams were chill and can be studied for reliably with review material.

Nice guy and clearly very knowledgeable. Due to accent unfortunately not a great lecturer, however slides are clear and helpful. Most of this class ended up being self study due to the nature of learning a coding language. Homework is easy if you allocate enough time, and exams aren't bad.

Avoid this professor if you're unfamiliar with OOP or only know Python; you'll struggle to keep up. Thankfully, with OOP and Java experience, switching to C++ was manageable. Expect written class participation tests 3 times in a single class. TAs are helpful, so ask them questions. Start HWs second-half assignments are very time-consuming.

I honestly didn't pay attention a single day in this class (if I went at all). 120 is a very very easy class and all the material is pretty much the same for every prof. He has an accent, but it's not hard to make out what he's saying
decent prof, csce 120 is pretty common so the only thing that matters is getting a good lab time, finding a friend group, and studying for exams.
